Collaboration with Chatbots or other AI Tools

MAYBE

Discouraged
for most purposes.
Forbidden
for code-level work.

For several reasons, we do not allow the use of these tools for writing code in 6.101:
(1) reading, writing, and understanding code without AI assistance remain essential skills;
(2) we believe AI assistance is used most effectively by practitioners who know how to construct correct, efficient, well-organized software
without
AI help;
and (3) pedagogically, we believe that learning how to develop algorithms, write code, and debug it "by hand" is the most effective way to develop a solid understanding of programming fundamentals and problem-solving strategies.

This means
you cannot use AI tools to write code or to improve code you have written
.
You cannot consult code provided to you by an AI tool, and since these tools are often engineered to respond with code even when a prompt does not request it, it is your responsibility to prevent such interactions.
As with help from other people, your use of AI tools
must not involve step-by-step, algorithmic instructions either in code or at a code level
.
And as with an over-eager pset partner who wants to show you their clever solution to the lab, it is your responsibility to shut down such conversations and write your own code. Note that some code editors are set up to use AI out-of-the-box; if your editor does this, it is your responsibility to disable those features.

Using generative AI tools to write text or code

NO

No automatic code generation.

like ChatGPT)
AI Tools: See below for detailed policy.

AI Tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Github Copilot) Policy
Quizzes and Final Exam: All AI tools are prohibited.
Assignments/Labs: AI tools may be used for syntax help, debugging tips, or general
programming questions, but not for generating or completing solutions.
If you use an AI tool, you must include a statement in your submission with:
The name of the tool used
A transcript or export of your interaction with the tool
If in doubt, ask the instructor before using an AI tool.

Within this class, you are welcome to use foundation models (ChatGPT, Gemini, DALL-E, Claude,
Midjourney, GitHub Copilot, etc.) in an unrestricted fashion. However, please note that Large
Language Models (LLMs) have a tendency to hallucinate incorrect facts and fake citations. Simi-
larly, code generation models may produce inaccurate or insecure output.
You remain fully responsible for any inaccurate, biased, offensive, or otherwise unethical
content you submit, regardless of whether it originated from you or a foundation model. If you
use a foundation model, its contribution must be acknowledged in your submission; failure to do
so will result in a penalty. Despite these disclaimers, the use of foundation models is encouraged,
as they can enable you to produce higher-quality work in less time.

During the project only, students are free to use outside resources (e.g., coding blog
posts or guides, YouTube tutorials, generative AI, etc.) to help complete assigned coding
tasks. However, you must be able to explain and validate any code you produce, and
you must credit all sources and collaborators. Failure to do so will be considered
cheating.

It is ok to talk to other students or online resources (e.g., generative AI tools) about general
solution techniques for assignments, but it is not ok to copy solutions in part or as a whole.
Plagiarism will result in a loss of marks and/or fingers for all guilty students involved.

You are welcome to use AI-tools to help you program.
Beware, the programs generated by AI-tools often do not meet the requirements of CSC120, e.g.,
they might use programing techniques or constructs other than what has been taught in the course
up to that point (which is not permitted - see the

Laboratory Tasks
instructions).
Your work must also demonstrate the required

Programming Style
, and AI-generated code often is nasty nasty nasty.

You may choose to use generative AI in your projects. If you select this option, you may use AI only after Project 4 and Exam 1 and you must work independently, and not with another classmate.
If your code is similar to code submitted by another student, we will move forward with academic integrity proceedings.
Claiming that your code was generated by AI will not be considered a valid excuse. You should keep in mind that AI tools sometimes generate fairly unusual solutions, and code that might be
similar to code generated by others using similar prompts. You should get the other idea and write it in your own way even if the code works.

You should never submit a code that is not yours even if you received that code from a TA or from any Generative AI.

Utilizing AI Coding Tools

You may choose to take advantage of AI tools that support software development, such as ChatGPT. If you select this option, you may use this option only after Project 4 and Exam 1 and you must work independently, and not with another student.
We do not provide explicit support or training in the use of these tools. Sometimes we provide some videos to guide you on how to use them. However, you may find them helpful, both now and in the future.

A few notes if you choose this option:

Your code will still be checked for plagiarism. If you submit code that is highly-similar to code submitted by another student, we will move forward with academic integrity proceedings.
Claiming that your code was generated by AI will not be considered a valid excuse. You should keep in mind that AI tools sometimes generate fairly unusual solutions, and code that might be
similar to code generated by others using similar prompts.

Course staff will not assist you if you do not understand your own code. Do not ask AI to complete a portion of the code and then come to the helproom for support if you don't understand
what it generated. Debugging and understanding code generated by AI is part of the challenge of using these tools.

Quizzes and Exams will cover both coding and conceptual content. You will be expected to complete these questions unaided during the allowed time.
Relying on AI to finish your assignments will affect your performance in the exams.
The objective of the class is to teach code reading, code writing, and ability to identify and rectify errors.

If you have questions about this option, please ask on the forum or come to the instructors office hours.

The use of generative AI tools or AI-assisted code editors (e.g. ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, Cursor, etc.) is permitted only in the same contexts where collaboration with another person is allowed, following the guidelines above. For example:

Allowed Use

Prohibited Use

Learning course concepts, generating examples of a particular coding pattern, interactively checking your knowledge, etc.

Generating project code, test cases, or any other work to be submitted (with or without modifications)

Understanding compiler errors or getting suggestions for debugging a problem

Exhaustively proofreading your code to find and/or correct any mistakes

Brainstorming and identifying potential edge cases for testing

Asking for a list of test cases (even if they aren't written out as code)

Generating additional practice exam questions or other use for studying

Using generative AI tools during exams

Additionally, the use of generative AI in a deceptive or malicious fashion is prohibited. This includes but is not limited to:

Impersonating yourself or others in course contexts, for example in emails, virtual office hours, or online course forums.

Passing off generated content as your own work when contributing to group assignments.

Using generative AI to facilitate harassment of others.
Copying solutions in whole or in part (including from the Internet, an AI bot, etc.), even if the solution is modified

Generative AI Usage

It is critical for your learning in this class that you get the opportunity to practice the material by working through problems with your peers or with your instructors during office hours. Your course instructors are prepared to provide the right level of guidance to help you work your way toward a solution while still ensuring you are learning the material. ChatGPT and other Generative AI systems may seem like a convenient resource for homework tips and suggestions, but they lack the nuance needed to provide the right level of guidance and are likely to give you too much (and possibly incorrect answers), thereby eliminating your opportunity to actually learn the material. For that reason, you are not permitted to consult with Generative AI on current homework problems at all.

There are other use cases, however, that we think are more appropriate. Any time you engage with it, make sure to confirm it is giving you accurate information. Generative AI is still prone to hallucinations and may well feed you false information. Try not to trust its answers too much.

You may use AI tools:

... to explain a general concept to you

... for additional practice problems

... to give you more detail on an
already-published homework solution
from a previous week's homework

... to grade your homework
after the deadline has passed

... whether it thinks your graded solution should earn more points on our rubric

You may not use AI tools:

... how to solve a homework problem for the current week

... for hints on a homework problem for the current week

... to grade your homework before the deadline has passed (even if you have already submitted it)

Artificial intelligence (AI) language models, such as ChatGPT, and online assignment help tools, such as Chegg® are examples of online learning support platforms that can not be used to solve assessments in this course. The following actions are not allowed in this course:

Submitting all or any part of an assignment statement to an online learning support platform

Incorporating AI generated responses of parts in an assignment

Using AI to brainstorm, formulate arguments, or template ideas for assignments

Using AI to summarize or contextualize source materials

Submitting your own work for this class to an online learning support platform for iteration or improvement

The reason why it is not possible to use tools like ChatGPT is because the objective of this course is for you to learn in detail the steps characterizing design, development, and testing of fairly large programs. If you are in doubt as to whether you are using an online learning support platform appropriately in this course, I encourage you to discuss your situation with me.
